steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
Using the sales data you cleaned in Work 1, you'll draft a report for the CEO. Much faster than starting from a blank page.

Today you'll learn five new things.

  1. Say who reads it, how long, and what tone
  2. Get an outline first, not the full text
  3. Get the draft as a file
  4. Ask for changes to parts you don't like
  5. Check the numbers, and finish it yourself
  • Time: 20 minutes
  • You need: sales_clean.csv from Work 1

steps.title: Check your material
steps.html: Open the Practice folder on your desktop and look for sales_clean.csv, the clean copy you made in Work 1.

check.q: Is sales_clean.csv in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If you don't have sales_clean.csv
steps.html:
We recommend doing Work 1 first. To jump in now:

  1. Download the sample sales.csv and move it into Practice.
  2. Tell Claude: "From sales.csv, remove the duplicate row, change 'Gang nam' to 'Gangnam', fill the blank Qty with Amount ÷ UnitPrice, and save it as sales_clean.csv."

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html: Claude app → Code tab → + New. Check the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.

steps.title: Give context, get an outline first
steps.html: The secret to a good draft is context: who reads it, how long, what tone. And get an outline first, not the full text. (Same idea as Plan in Desktop 5.)
steps.alt: Given the context, Claude suggests a report outline first
steps.code: I'm writing a November sales-by-branch report from sales_clean.csv. It's for the CEO, one page, formal tone. Don't write it yet; suggest an outline first

check.q: Did you get an outline you're happy with?

steps.title: If you want to change the outline
steps.html:
Just say what you want. For example:

  • "Drop the item notes and add 'what went well and what didn't, by branch'"
  • "Put the summary first, and only 3 suggestions"

Adjust it as many times as you like. This is the cheapest moment to set the direction.

steps.title: Get the draft as a file
steps.html: The create-file card shows the start of the draft. Read it and click Allow. Then open nov-sales-report.txt in Practice and read it all the way through.
steps.alt: A create-file permission card for the report draft
steps.code: Great. Write the report draft from that outline and save it as nov-sales-report.txt

check.q: Was nov-sales-report.txt created, and did you read it?

steps.title: If the file wasn't created
steps.html:
• If you denied the card, send it again and allow it.
  • If Claude only wrote it in the chat, say "Save the draft you just wrote as nov-sales-report.txt."

steps.title: Ask for changes to parts you don't like
steps.html: Drafts are meant to be edited. Don't have it rewrite everything; point to exactly what to change. Read the red and green lines on the card, then allow.
steps.code: Cut the summary at the top to 3 lines, and change the suggestions to just 3 practical actions

check.q: Did you check the changes on the card and allow them?

steps.title: If you don't like the edit
steps.html:
• Deny it on the card and ask again. (Desktop 2)
  • If you already allowed it: "Undo what you just changed." (Desktop 6)
  • For tone, be specific: "A bit more concise, in report style."

steps.title: Check the report's numbers
steps.html:
Wrong numbers are the most embarrassing mistake in a report. Have Claude check, and verify at least one yourself.

Correct: total 696.50; Gangnam 277.00 · Hongdae 266.50 · Busan 153.00
steps.code: Check each number in the report against sales_clean.csv, one by one. Tell me if any are wrong

steps.title: If a number was wrong
steps.html: Say "Fix the wrong numbers using sales_clean.csv," read the card and allow it. As in Work 1, check once more against a number you know (total 696.50).

steps.title: You finish it
steps.html:
Think of an AI draft as 70–80% done. You fill in the rest.

  • Add context the AI doesn't know, e.g. "Busan was closed for two weeks of renovation in November."
  • Check it didn't state guesses as facts. If it asserted causes that aren't in the data ("because of the weather"), delete them or mark them as guesses.
  • If your company has a template, paste the content into it in Word and polish it there.
Your name goes on the report. Always read it through yourself one last time.

steps.title: 🎉 Work practice 3 done! What you learned
steps.html:
From cleaned data to a report draft, without ever facing a blank page.

Give context→Outline first→Draft file→Targeted edits→Check numbers · you finish

Good things to say when asking for a report

Who reads it"for the CEO", "for my team", "for customers"
Length"one page", "under 5 lines"
Tone"formal", "concise report style"
Material"from sales_clean.csv", "using notice-summary.txt"

Wrapping up Work 1–3

Clean up (Work 1) → summarize (Work 2) → report (Work 3). With this flow you can finish monthly reporting much faster. Next up: turning meeting recordings into a work log.
